title: RuntimeAdapter
description: C6 (draft): wire protocol between the core and an agent runtime: a runtime adapter (a plugin of a foreign runtime, which may be Python) or the engine `ulei-engine`. The runtime is the server and serves the operations in `x-methods`; the core and other local callers are clients: each is `POST /v1/<name>` with the input as the JSON body over HTTP/1.1 on a unix socket, one request per connection; a `200` answer carries the output and any other status carries `Error` (`x-transport`, `x-error`, ADR-0008). Methods: `inject`, `is_idle`, `status`, `submit_turn`, `turn_events`, `interrupt`, `set_route`, `skills_dir`, `mcp_register`, `raw_sessions`, `owner_channel`, `inbox_turns`, `report_delivery`; session and turn semantics: ADR-0028; a turn's reply: ADR-0031.

x-methods.name: inject
x-methods.description: Idempotent on `event_id`: the runtime keeps a record of every accepted event across its restarts and answers a recorded `event_id` with the recorded `session_id` and `turn` and starts nothing, unless the `attempt` is higher and the recorded turn's delivery was `silent`, which is a new delivery; a recorded turn the runtime no longer holds reads `unknown` (ADR-0037 section 3).

x-transport.protocol: HTTP/1.1 with JSON bodies over a SOCK_STREAM unix socket; the runtime (adapter or engine) listens, the client (the core or another local caller) connects
x-transport.request: `POST /v1/<name>` with the method input as the body; `Content-Length` required, `Transfer-Encoding` refused
x-transport.response: `200` with the method output as the body; every other status with `Error` as the body; `Content-Type: application/json`, `Content-Length`, `Connection: close`
x-transport.connection: one request per connection; the server closes after its answer
x-transport.peer_check: each side refuses a peer whose SO_PEERCRED uid differs from its own effective uid; the client checks before it sends any byte

Error.description: Body of every non-200 answer. `message` is a short diagnostic that never echoes the payload.

ErrorCode.description: Error class; the HTTP status of each is fixed in ADR-0008.

InjectRequest.description: Inject an inbox event (C1) into the runtime's owner session when that session is free: no turn runs, none is queued and the runtime can deliver the turn's answer to the owner (for the engine: ADR-0036 section 5). Idempotent on `event_id`: the runtime keeps a record of every accepted event across its restarts and answers a recorded `event_id` with the recorded `session_id` and `turn` and starts nothing, unless the `attempt` is higher and the recorded turn's delivery was `silent`, which is a new delivery; a recorded turn the runtime no longer holds reads `unknown` (ADR-0037 section 3).

prompt.description: The model text the core built from the event (ADR-0036 section 4), run unchanged as the prompt of the event turn (untrusted data).

lease.description: Inbox lease of the core's claim. Data only: the runtime never calls the inbox, never acks and never settles the event.

attempt.description: Delivery attempt: C1 `Row.attempts` of the core's claim. An `attempt` of a recorded `event_id` that is not higher than the recorded one answers the recorded turn and starts nothing, and so does a higher one unless the recorded turn's delivery was `silent`; a higher `attempt` after a recorded `silent` delivery is a new delivery and a new turn.

accepted.description: The runtime took the event into a turn.

session_id.description: Session that received the event: the session key for the engine. Present when accepted.

retry_after_s.description: Busy: retry after this many seconds. Present when not accepted.

turn.description: The turn that received the event; present when accepted.

IdleStatus.description: Whether the owner's session, the one `inject` targets, is free: no turn runs, none is queued and the runtime can deliver the turn's answer to the owner (for the engine: ADR-0036 section 5).

since.description: Unix time since when it is idle.

channel.description: A channel holds `inbox_turns` for the owner session, or follows the inbox turn of that hold that the session runs. The engine always sends it; a runtime without `inbox_turns` omits it.

SessionKey.description: Session key: the engine's `--session` name and C8 `Session.key`. It names the key's current session; the engine creates the session on the key's first turn.

RouteAlias.description: A qb route alias, as C4G `TurnRequest.route`.

TurnId.description: Identity of one accepted turn, given when the turn is accepted, queued or started, and never given to another turn of the same runtime, across restarts.

TurnState.description: Where a turn is: `queued` waits in its session's queue, `running` runs, `ended` ran to an `outcome`, `dropped` left the queue by `interrupt` without running, `unknown` the runtime does not hold this turn (never accepted, or its report is gone).

TurnOutcome.description: How an ended turn ended: `completed` the model answered and stopped, `max_steps` the turn reached its step limit, `halted` a policy ended the turn, `interrupted` `interrupt` stopped it, `context_exhausted` compaction could not make a step fit, `quota_exhausted` every login of the route is out of quota, `failed` any other gateway, transport or runtime failure.

Delivery.description: What the channel did with an inbox turn's answer (ADR-0036 sections 6 and 7): `sent` sent and confirmed for every part, `send_failed` a send not confirmed, `silent` a silence marker, `silent_done` the marker `NO_REPLY_DONE`, `no_answer` the turn did not consume its event.

TurnReport.description: One turn as the runtime holds it.

outcome.description: How the turn ended; present when `state` is `ended`, except in a `last_turn` read back from the journal after a runtime restart, which does not hold it.

ended.description: Unix time the turn ended or was dropped; present for `ended` and `dropped`, except in a `last_turn` read back from the journal after a runtime restart, which does not hold it.

line.description: The one line an ended turn reports instead of an answer: for `quota_exhausted` the route and its nearest reset in UTC, for `context_exhausted` and `failed` the reason. Absent for the other outcomes.

delivery.description: What the channel did with the answer; present only on an `ended` inbox turn the channel reported.

StatusRequest.description: Read the state of one session and, with `turn`, of one of its turns.

turn.description: A turn of the session to report as `turn` of the answer.

SessionStatus.description: State of one session. A key without a session reads idle with an empty queue and no turn.

running.description: A turn of the session is running.

since.description: Unix time since when the session is running or idle: the start of the running turn, the end of the last turn, or the runtime's start.

queue_depth.description: Turns waiting in the session's queue.

route.description: The route alias the session's next turn runs on: the one `set_route` stored, else the runtime's default.

last_turn.description: The turn that ended last; absent before the first one. After a runtime restart and before a turn of the session ends, the last turn the journal holds, named by the journal (ADR-0028 section 4).

turn.description: The turn the request named; present when it named one.

SubmitTurnRequest.description: Run one owner prompt as one turn of a session: at once when the session is idle, else after the turns queued before it.

prompt.description: The owner's prompt, the user message of the turn.

channel.description: The channel the prompt came on, as the engine's `--channel`.

new.description: Start a new session of the key for this turn, as the engine's `--new`, when the turn starts; the previous session stays in the journal. Absent means false.

context.description: Context for the model on this turn only: appended to the copy of the prompt each request of the turn sends, never journaled. Absent means none.

images.description: Images the owner attached to the prompt, in arrival order (ADR-0089): absolute paths of local files the runtime reads. The engine attaches each as an image block after the prompt's text in the copy of the prompt each request of the turn sends, and journals the prompt without them. Absent means none.

message_id.description: The channel's id of the owner message the prompt answers, the last one of a coalesced batch (ADR-0088): the message `react_to_message` reacts to when the model names none. Absent for a turn without one, such as a reaction wake-up.

SubmitTurnResponse.description: Result of `submit_turn`. A full queue refuses the prompt: `accepted` false and `queue_depth` 32.

accepted.description: The turn started or joined the queue.

turn.description: The accepted turn; present when accepted.

position.description: 0 when the turn started, else its place in the queue from 1; present when accepted.

queue_depth.description: Turns waiting in the session's queue after the call.

TurnEventsRequest.description: Read the events of one turn after `after`. The answer is held until the turn has an event after `after`, and given at once when it already has one or will have no more (`ended`, `dropped`, `unknown`).

after.description: The `seq` of the last event the caller holds; 0 for none.

TurnEventType.description: Kind of a turn event: `start` the turn starts running; `interim` an assistant message while the turn runs; `final` the turn's answer; `reaction` the agent set an emoji reaction on a channel message; `end` the turn ended with an `outcome`; `dropped` the turn left the queue by `interrupt` without running. A turn that runs has `start`, then any `interim`, then any `reaction`, then at most one `final`, then `end`; a dropped turn has only `dropped`.

TurnEvent.description: One event of a turn: `seq`, `type` and the payload of that type (`interim` and `final`: `text`; `reaction`: `message_id` and the emoji in `text`; `end`: `outcome` and, for `quota_exhausted`, `context_exhausted` and `failed`, `line`).

seq.description: Place of the event in its turn, from 1, without gaps.

text.description: The assistant's visible text (`interim`, `final`) or the emoji of a `reaction`; never empty.

message_id.description: The channel's id of the message the agent reacted to (`reaction`).

TurnEventsPage.description: Result of `turn_events`: the turn's events after the request's `after`, in order, as many as fit the body limit and at least one when the turn has one.

state.description: Where the turn is when the answer is given.

events.description: The events, oldest first; empty when the turn has no event after `after` and will have no more, or when a later request for the turn released this one.

InboxTurnsRequest.description: Wait for the next inbox turn of the owner session (ADR-0036 section 5). The answer is held until an inbox turn not yet handed over exists, and given at once when one does.

InboxTurns.description: Result of `inbox_turns`: the oldest inbox turn not yet handed over.

turn.description: The inbox turn; absent only when a newer request released the hold.

DeliveryReport.description: Report what the channel did with the answer of a handed-over inbox turn that has ended. `Ack.ok` is true when the runtime stored it, false for any other turn or a second report.

InterruptRequest.description: Stop the running turn of a session at once; the session and its history stay.

InterruptResponse.description: Result of `interrupt`. An idle session answers `interrupted` false and changes nothing.

interrupted.description: This call interrupted the running turn. False for an idle session and for a turn an earlier `interrupt` already interrupted that is still unwinding; such a call changes nothing.

dropped.description: The queued turn that was next and was dropped; absent when the queue was empty.

queue_depth.description: Turns left in the session's queue; they run in order after the interrupted turn.

SetRouteRequest.description: Run the session's later turns on a route alias. Stored with the session (C8 `Session.route`) until a new session of the key.

RouteSet.description: Result of `set_route`: the alias in force for the session's next turn.

McpServer.description: Register the core MCP facade (C2) in the runtime.

RawSessionsQuery.description: Read the runtime's raw dialogue, the source of the archive (ADR-0051 section 3): the messages turns appended, live and archived, after the cursor in journal order. The engine leaves out compaction messages, steps, system prompts, a turn's context and delivery records; forget marks filter nothing.

since.description: Only messages written at or after this Unix time; a message without a time matches no time filter.

until.description: Only messages written at or before this Unix time; a message without a time matches no time filter.

limit.description: Maximum messages, the skipped ones of `RawSessionsPage.skipped` included; absent means 10000. A page holds fewer when the next message would take the answer over `max_body_bytes`.

cursor.description: Cursor from the previous page; absent reads from the first message. The engine's cursor is the journal position `n` of the page's last message in decimal.

skipped.description: Messages of the page that do not fit an answer of `max_body_bytes` alone, named without their text or bytes, oldest first; the cursor moves past them as past the served ones. Absent when the page skips none.

cursor.description: Next cursor; absent at the end.

RawSkipped.description: A raw message the runtime leaves out of its page because the message alone would take the answer over `max_body_bytes`.

session_key.description: Key of the session. The engine always sends it.

seq.description: Position in the session, C8 `Message.seq`. The engine always sends it.

ts.description: Unix time the message was written; absent when the runtime did not record it.

len.description: Bytes of the stored message as `RawMessage.message` would carry it.

session_id.description: Session id; the engine's is C8 `Session.id` in decimal.

session_key.description: Key of the session. The engine always sends it.

seq.description: Position in the session, C8 `Message.seq`. The engine always sends it.

ts.description: Unix time the message was written; absent when the runtime did not record it.

role.description: Role, e.g. `user`, `assistant`, `tool`; the engine's is the role of its history index.

content.description: Text content; the engine's is the text of its history index.

message.description: The stored message as it was written, a C4G `Message` in its canonical C4G serialization (C8 `Message.message`). The engine always sends it.

OwnerChannel.description: The owner's channel as the runtime knows it. Opaque to the core.
